mechanism_narrative: The sharp rebound in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT from t-2w to t-0w signals a return of commuting and downtown foot traffic. That should lift discretionary shopping visits and push RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks relative to the prior four-week average.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -59.9 to -27.6 and TRANSIT from -65.1 to -50.4 by t-0w
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain near or below their t-0w levels yet RETAIL_REC does not rise above the prior 4-week mean over the next 28 days, the mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility stays elevated and WORKPLACES remain depressed, people substitute toward local errands and short neighborhood trips rather than destination shopping. This should keep RETAIL_REC below its recent four-week average over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays above +10 and WORKPLACES stays below -20 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed positive from t-3w to t-0w while WORKPLACES stayed negative
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL remains above +10 with WORKPLACES below -20 for two weeks and RETAIL_REC still rises over the next 14 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A renewed tightening phase that depresses TRANSIT below its recent level acts quickly on discretionary shopping because trips to retail corridors are curtailed first. This should produce a lower RETAIL_REC mean within one week of the downturn.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -60 after having improved for at least one week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -65.1 at t-2w to -50.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: If TRANSIT drops below -60 after a short improvement and RETAIL_REC does not fall within the following 7 days, the claim is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained weakness in PARKS during warm-weather weeks signals fewer leisure outings and weaker general outing intensity. That spillover lowers retail-and-recreation visits over the next four weeks, even if grocery trips are more stable.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS remained negative across all four weekly means and improved only partially at t-0w
failure_condition: If PARKS stays negative but RETAIL_REC exceeds its prior 4-week mean over the next 28 days, the mechanism is false.

mechanism_narrative: An upswing in GROCERY_PHARM relative to PARKS indicates more essential errands and fewer discretionary outings. That mix usually precedes weaker shopping visits, so RETAIL_REC should fall over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises by at least 8 points week-on-week while PARKS does not rise
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM recovered from -24.3 to -13.4 while PARKS stayed negative
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM rises by 8 or more points without a PARKS recovery and RETAIL_REC does not decline within 14 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A continued rebound in WORKPLACES is a leading signal of restored weekday routine. Once WORKPLACES improves for two straight weeks, retail visits should follow with a lag and RETAIL_REC should be higher over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES improves for two consecutive weeks and crosses above -40
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -59.9 at t-2w to -27.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES remains improved for two weeks and RETAIL_REC does not exceed the previous 4-week mean over the next 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain deeply negative, access constraints and reduced commuting jointly suppress shopping trips. The combined effect should keep RETAIL_REC below its recent average over a one-week horizon.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT stays below -50 and WORKPLACES stays below -25 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT was -50.4 and WORKPLACES was -27.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: If TRANSIT stays below -50 and WORKPLACES below -25 for a week but RETAIL_REC does not fall within 7 days, the mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained improvement in PARKS combined with easing TRANSIT indicates broader weekend and leisure mobility returning. That spillover should raise RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks unless park mobility stalls again.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 10 points and TRANSIT rises by at least 5 points over two weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -38.4 to -24.9 while TRANSIT improved from -60.4 to -50.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: If PARKS and TRANSIT both improve as specified but RETAIL_REC does not rise above its prior 4-week mean over the next 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.
